title: Ruum-User token claims
description: The claims of the signed token that the app gateway sends to an app in the header `Ruum-User` (docs/DESIGN.md section 9.4; the design text calls it `Platform-User`). A JWT (EdDSA) signed with the platform's app-token keys (`https://ruum.space/.well-known/app-jwks.json`, a key set apart from the API keys). The app checks it with the Ruum SDK: signature, `iss`, `aud` = its own app ID, `exp`. It holds only the facts this app may know. It is made for each request (or cached for at most 5 seconds), so a removed role stops working at once; the app should not keep its own copy of roles. The same format identifies calls from other apps (`actor: app`, design 9.10) and from partners (`actor: partner`). DRAFT for review (step 3 specify phase, docs/STEP3.md).

iss.description: The laptop stack uses `https://ruum.localhost`; the SDK takes the issuer from `RUUM_ISSUER`.

aud.description: `app:<app-node-id>`. A preview gets the same audience; `env` tells them apart.

sub.description: `pairwise:<id>`: a person or an agent, stable for this app and different for every other app, so two apps cannot join their user lists. `app:<id>`: a calling app of the same tenant. `partner:<key-id>`: a partner API key. `anonymous:<visit>`: a visitor of a public app without sign-in.

name.description: Only if the manifest asks (`claims`) and the tenant allows.

email.description: Only if the manifest asks and the tenant allows (never for public apps by default).

roles.description: The app roles of the visitor (design 9.3): explicit grants of active roles, or the default role for a visitor with `view` and no explicit role. Empty for anonymous visitors and partners.

node_roles.description: The visitor's effective rights on the bound nodes, by binding name, for UI decisions (`{"db": "edit"}`). Not a grant: the app's own access goes through its bindings.

actor.description: Who sends the request. `agent`: an agent acting for a user (its user's pairwise ID is `on_behalf_of`).

on_behalf_of.description: The user that an agent or a calling app acts for (a delegation chain, design 9.10).

chain.description: The apps of a delegation chain, oldest first (user → app A → app B: B sees `["app:<A>"]`).

scopes.description: For `app` and `partner` actors: the API scopes of the binding or the key.
